title: Exclusive: Mossimo Giannulli Requests Unexpected Spousal Support in Lori Loughlin Divorce Response
body:
Los Angeles – In a development that adds a new twist to the high‑profile split of former “College Cheer” star Lori Loughlin and fashion designer Mossimo Giannulli, the 63‑year‑old husband has filed a response that seeks a markedly different division of their marital estate. While Loughbin’s petition called for the couple’s assets, properties and liabilities to be allocated strictly according to their 1995 prenuptial agreement, Giannulli’s filing asks the court to deviate from that arrangement, arguing that the agreement no longer reflects the realities of their 28‑year marriage and the financial fallout from the 2019 college‑admissions scandal that brought both of them under intense legal scrutiny.

Giannulli’s response, filed in Los Angeles Superior Court, contends that the prenuptial contract—crafted before the couple amassed the wealth that would later fund multiple homes, luxury vehicles and a sprawling business empire—fails to account for the substantial debts incurred after the fraud case. The couple was sentenced in 2020 to two months in prison and a $250,000 fine each, a judgment that led to the loss of several high‑value assets, including a $4 million Beverly Hills mansion that was later sold to satisfy creditors. Giannulli’s legal team argues that a strict enforcement of the original agreement would unfairly penalize him, leaving him with a disproportionate share of the remaining liabilities while Loughlin would retain the bulk of the residual wealth.

Legal experts note that prenuptial agreements, though generally upheld in California when voluntarily executed and free of duress, can be challenged if one party can demonstrate a material change in circumstances. “The courts look at whether the agreement still serves the equitable interests of both parties,” said Elena Martinez, a family‑law attorney who has followed the case. “Given the extraordinary financial turbulence caused by the admissions fraud conviction, Giannulli has a plausible argument that the original terms are no longer just.” However, Martinez cautioned that California’s community‑property laws typically favor an equal split of assets and debts accrued during the marriage, and a judge may be reluctant to rewrite a longstanding contract without compelling evidence.

The filing also reveals that Giannulli is seeking a temporary restraining order to prevent Loughlin from selling or otherwise disposing of any jointly owned property until the division of assets is finalized. This move underscores the contentious nature of the negotiations, which have been marked by public statements from both sides. Loughlin, who filed for divorce in early March, emphasized her desire to honor the prenuptial terms, describing them as “the roadmap we agreed upon before we ever imagined fame or scandal.” Giannulli, in contrast, has framed his request as a bid to achieve a “fair and realistic” settlement that reflects the couple’s current financial standing.

Industry observers point out that the dispute could have broader implications for celebrity couples who rely on pre‑marital contracts to safeguard their wealth. The high‑profile nature of the case, combined with the lingering public fascination with the college‑admissions scandal, means that any judicial ruling may set a precedent for how courts treat prenuptial agreements in the wake of criminal convictions that dramatically alter a couple’s financial landscape. “We may see a shift toward more flexible interpretations of these contracts when extraordinary events—like fraud convictions—reshape the parties’ economic reality,” said Michael Chen, a professor of entertainment law at USC Gould School of Law.

As both parties await a hearing date, the next steps will likely involve extensive financial disclosures and possibly a forensic accounting of the couple’s assets and debts. The court’s decision could determine whether Giannulli receives a larger share of the remaining estate or whether Loughlin’s request for a strict prenuptial split stands. Regardless of the outcome, the case underscores the complex interplay between celebrity, legal agreements and the unforeseen consequences of criminal proceedings.

Looking ahead, the resolution of this divorce will not only dictate the financial futures of Loughlin and Giannulli but may also influence how future celebrity marriages approach prenuptial planning, especially in an era where public scandals can swiftly upend even the most meticulously crafted agreements. The legal community, as well as fans of the former “Full House” star, will be watching closely as the courtroom drama unfolds.
